### application-core reuse R1: the native property cache, a property projection of the canonical claim in the existing proof store

change `sktkmnpnoqsv` · [log `e77a9a79565f`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/aa238023-596d-49bd-8039-52502ec096fc/e77a9a79565f6c97a8533e2a7f7f238645f3d119ad5aee7236e6154d3c10cd20.jsonl.gz)

prove --cache DIR now keeps a property check's verified and refuted results in the regression proofs' store (lib/src/reuse.rs), keyed by the same canonical claim digest. The claim projects the target's parameters, the closure of the target and of every constructor its inputs, result and declared exceptions are made with, the assumption, assertion, throws clauses, the meaning of \old, the null and alias choices, any construction plan, the bounds and the checker's settings. A first assumption marks it a property claim, so it never shares a key with a regression claim of the same target. Every field of property::Options is named in the projection; an unknown one, or an engine other than the own checker, refuses the check under --cache instead of keying without it. A verified hit gives back the stored outcome and statement, marked as reused. A refutation is stored with the harness it was found in, and reused only once its witness fails that harness again on the current classes. Nothing unresolved is stored.

Verified inline: lib/tests/reuse.rs (7 tests, on the frozen quote fixture and small builds, native engine, no JBMC): exact hits of both kinds, a stale stored witness proved again, an input's changed constructor invalidating the proof of an unchanged method (the test fails with the constructor roots taken out), a key per assertion, assumption, throws clause, domain, bound and plan history, none for an unrelated change. The contract's R1 now verifies cold and on the rerun; 230 unit tests, tests/application_core.rs and tests/summaries.rs pass, clippy is clean. Interface requests for property.rs and main.rs are under the stream brief's Progress.

### application-core reuse J3: a planned domain's plans and a modelled call's model in the claim key, digested whole as their strict types

change `mslqzrprorvn` · [log `bc9aa0450064`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/aa238023-596d-49bd-8039-52502ec096fc/bc9aa0450064232ed23f89ed22d9561a4991a0e835a1a07e8cff7c606c44b87c.jsonl.gz)

The claim key's projection (lib/src/spec/cache.rs) refused every claim with a planned domain or a call model as uncacheable, since Phase 0 added those parts without registering them. TYPED now names domain.made_by.before/after (construction plans) and environment.calls[].model (a call model): each is digested whole once it reads back exactly as its type of spec::plans, which refuses every undeclared field and variant, so nothing in them is left out of the key and an undeclared field still makes the claim uncacheable by name.

Verified inline: three new tests in lib/tests/reuse.rs. The 8 frozen claims of tests/fixtures/application-core each get a distinct key; 27 changes to their histories (setup calls, constructors, factories, setup bounds, one version's plan alone), model outcomes (results, exceptions, coupling, key, bound) and value bounds (String and list lengths, nullability, evidence levels, element kinds) each give a new key; undeclared fields, an unknown variant and a non-canonical plan are refused. The integration contract's J3 now passes on distinct keys instead of on the refusal. 230 unit tests and the contract, summaries, heap, effects and foundations suites pass.

Also recorded under Progress: an unsound regression-cache hit the objects stream found in proof_cache.rs (an inner object's constructor is missing from the closure's roots), which is this stream's next piece of work.

### application-core reuse: a regression claim's closure rooted at every constructor its harness calls, an inner object's included

change `qssovxorxqsy` · [log `76a89868444d`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/aa238023-596d-49bd-8039-52502ec096fc/76a89868444d0ef14c44507dd64f5cdb99d29e1b5d5e25cdc61e787a4c0658f1.jsonl.gz)

proof_cache::Regression::claim rooted each version's closure at a made object's own constructor only, not at the constructors of the objects it is made from, which the harness calls too. So a build that changed only an inner constructor reused another build's verified result: get(new Wrap(new Inner(v), k)), whose Inner constructor stores v + 1 in one build, reused a rewrite's proof though get returns one more. The objects stream found it (their ignored test an_inner_objects_constructor_is_part_of_the_cached_claim). The claim now roots both versions, and a previous version's receiver and records, at every constructor RecordType::constructors lists.

Reproducer first: tests/reuse.rs's an_inner_objects_constructor_in_either_version_is_part_of_a_regression_claim failed before the fix with an exact hit on the changed build. It now checks that a rewrite is verified and reused on an unchanged rerun, and that a change to the inner constructor after, and then before, misses the cache and is refuted. Also fixed: tests/reuse.rs compiled each build into a shared directory it removed first, so parallel tests could remove each other's classes. Each build is now compiled once per run. Verified inline: tests/reuse.rs (11 tests, three runs), the 230 unit tests, and the application_core, compare, effects, foundations, heap, observations and summaries suites. The proof_cache module doc and lib/README.md say which constructors are roots.

**Reply:**

I built and committed R1, the native property cache, as `sktkmnpn`. The commit check reports 0 errors and 0 warnings, and no job was needed: everything ran on the native checker in unit tests.

**What it does now:**
- `prove --cache DIR` stores property results in the same store the regression proofs use, under the same key; there is no second cache.
- The key covers:
  - the target's parameters by name;
  - the code of the target and of every constructor its inputs, result and declared exceptions are built from;
  - the assertion, assumption and throws clauses;
  - the null and alias choices, and any construction plan;
  - the bounds and the checker settings.
- A marker in every property claim keeps it from ever sharing a key with a regression claim on the same method.
- `--cache` refuses the check in two cases rather than leaving something out of the key:
  - the property options have a field the cache doesn't list (one another stream adds later);
  - the engine is not the native one.
- A verified hit returns the stored result and statement, marked as reused, and runs no checker.
- A stored refutation is used only after its witness fails the stored harness again on the current classes; otherwise the check runs again. Unresolved results are never stored.

**Tests:**
- 7 new tests in `lib/tests/reuse.rs` pass, and the contract's R1 row now verifies on the first run and on the rerun.
- The 230 unit tests and `tests/summaries.rs` pass, and clippy is clean.
